subject: Error getting worker: Error: Connection attempt was aborted.

messages.author: 9163edfb5d401ab3
messages.subject: Error getting worker: Error: Connection attempt was aborted.
parts:
Hi.

I've been using Shiny and Shiny server for a while now, running on 64 bit Ubuntu Server 12.04, and once the data behind the apps started increasing in size I've been stuck using the configurable-timeouts patch, and wasn't able to use the newer versions. Now, however, I upgraded to shiny-server 0.4.0.8 according to the new installation guide, and once I try to load any of the apps, or examples provided, I get the following error:

[INFO] shiny-server - Error getting worker: Error: Connection attempt was aborted.

The logs are empty and I find no more information

I tried doing a fresh installation of Ubuntu with the same results.


What is there to do (and what more information required)?

messages.subject: Re: Error getting worker: Error: Connection attempt was aborted.
parts:
Gunnar,

When you say the log files are empty, are you referring to the log files in /var/log/shiny-server/* ? If not, can you check in that directory and see if there are any log files there? They would be the files that contain information about why a worker might be crashing before anyone's able to connect to it.

If no luck there, can you try logging in as the shiny user (sudo su shiny) and opening R and trying to run a Shiny application manually? For example, open R, run `library(shiny)`, and then `runApp(launch.browser=FALSE, port=1234)` then see if the application can open there?

Thanks,
Jeff

parts:
Those are the logs I'm referring to, all of them are empty.

The example apps behave well when run directly from R as you suggested.

While writing this, I found the cause of the error, however I find it so unusual... I had the run_as root directive instead of run_as shiny.
The server crashed if it was run_as root but works perfectly when run_as shiny. Upgrading to this new version also fixed my other issue (which I saw in some other posts), when I started proxying through an SSL connection no response from server.R appeared to get through. This update fixed that.

I don't understand how this can cause the application to fail, but I should've been running as shiny anyway...

Thank you so much for your time!

parts:
I have one question though. In the logfile /var/log/shiny-server.log I always get the warning:

[WARN] shiny-server - Running as root unnecessarily is a security risk! You could be running more securely as non-root.

But shiny user is not allowed to start upstart scripts, so I added the "setuid shiny" line into the upstart script /etc/init/shiny-server.conf according to the upstart cookbook.

Then I had to move the pidfile to a location where shiny user has write permissions, I created folder /var/run/shiny-server and gave shiny user ownership. I also had to move the logfile /etc/log/shiny-server.log to a directory with write permissions, so I just moved it in with the other logfiles in /etc/log/shiny-server.

So my question is:
am I doing it wrong?

messages.author: 9711d30301c32133
messages.subject: Re: Error getting worker: Error: Connection attempt was aborted.
parts:
Gunnar,

Thanks for pointing that out. I'm going to log that as a bug.

In Shiny Server Pro, it's required that you run the shiny-server process as root in order to properly collect metrics for the admin interface, so we shouldn't be emitting that warning. You should indeed be running shiny-server as root, and then have a "run_as" directive to specify that Shiny apps should be run as the Shiny user.

Sorry for the misleading log message.

Jeff
